title: Economic growth is experienced as an inaccessible ladder when jobs, networks and social norms block movement into a stable middle class
source_unit: World Bank, Voices of Europe and Central Asia: New Insights on Shared Prosperity and Jobs
geography: 43 communities in nine Europe and Central Asia countries: Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kyrgyz Republic, Serbia, Tajikistan and Türkiye

observations.period: 2016; qualitative account of growth and lived prosperity

denominator.unit: Structured focus groups and semi-structured interviews in 43 communities; qualitative participant denominator and selection frame are not summarized on the public page

growth_experience_gap.value: Residents report discontent and concern about a disappearing middle class despite overall economic growth and shared-prosperity gains

mobility_ladder.value: Many people see no open path to climb above the first rungs of an economic ladder

polarization.value: Men and women describe societies as increasingly polarized, with frustration about slow progress and unequal opportunity

observations.method: Structured focus-group discussions and semi-structured in-depth interviews across 43 communities in nine countries, used to complement quantitative poverty and mobility measures.
observations.uncertainty: Qualitative evidence reveals mechanisms and meanings rather than population prevalence; communities and participants are not a probability sample of Europe and Central Asia.
observations.subgroup: Men and women in selected communities across the nine participating countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Perceived stagnation may reflect rising expectations and comparison with fast gains at the top rather than absolute deterioration for every household.

observations.period: 2016; jobs as the link between growth and household mobility

denominator.unit: Qualitative participants across 43 communities; no pooled respondent denominator reported on the public page

job_quality.value: Stable, full-time, formal jobs with open contracts are widely associated with middle-class status and upward mobility

job_access.value: Good jobs, particularly for women and youth, are perceived as out of reach for a large share of people

downward_spiral.value: Access to jobs is described as capable of propelling households upward or precipitating a downward spiral

public_sector_aspiration.value: The vast majority still aspire to a public-sector job

observations.method: Cross-community qualitative inquiry into employment, mobility aspirations and household living standards.
observations.uncertainty: The report captures perceived job pathways and status meanings; it does not estimate the share of workers in each job category or establish that public-sector employment is objectively more mobile.
observations.subgroup: Women, youth and other community residents discussing work and mobility in the participating countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Public-sector aspirations may express demand for predictable rules, benefits and dignity where private-sector work is insecure, rather than nostalgia for state employment itself.

observations.period: 2016; networks and social norms as non-traditional employment barriers

denominator.unit: Qualitative participants across 43 communities; no pooled respondent denominator reported on the public page

network_barrier.value: Lack of professional and social networks and connections emerges as an important barrier to getting a job

social_norm_barrier.value: Social norms, especially those affecting women and youth, constrain access to opportunity

control_perception.value: Barriers perceived as beyond individual control generate frustration and hopelessness

policy_toolkit.value: The report calls for interventions addressing non-traditional barriers rather than relying only on macroeconomic or skills policy

observations.method: Qualitative interviews and focus groups designed to surface social norms, connections, attitudes and aspirations that conventional labor-market statistics miss.
observations.uncertainty: Network and norm barriers are reported perceptions and mechanisms; the study does not rank their causal importance against skills, discrimination, transport, vacancies or wages.
observations.subgroup: Men and women, including youth, in the participating communities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Networks can provide legitimate information and support in thin labor markets, but when access depends on family or political connections they can also reproduce exclusion and perceived unfairness.

observations.period: 2016; qualitative data as a correction to macroeconomic success narratives

denominator.unit: World Bank qualitative study in 43 communities; no pooled respondent denominator reported on the public page

performance_perception_disconnect.value: Traditional economic indicators can show growth and poverty reduction while people report no improvement in daily life or mobility

diagnostics_toolkit.value: The report recommends combining quantitative and qualitative work to identify networks, norms, attitudes and aspirations

decision_effect.value: Perceptions of how people get ahead and find good jobs can influence how they evaluate situations and make decisions

middle_class_meaning.value: Middle-class identity is tied to stable employment and earnings, not only measured income or consumption

observations.method: Mixed-methods methodological argument grounded in community focus groups, interviews and comparison with conventional indicators.
observations.uncertainty: The report’s qualitative account cannot determine the prevalence or political consequences of the perception gap across the full region.
observations.subgroup: Residents of selected communities and policymakers interpreting regional mobility and jobs data.
observations.counterinterpretation: Perception gaps can be temporary during rapid transition or crisis, but persistent gaps may signal that formal indicators omit security, agency, status and access dimensions of welfare.

related_sources.claim: World Bank regional publication page with expanded description of the qualitative research and the performance-perception disconnect.
Official World Bank main report PDF used for retrieval verification and hashing.

boundary: This record adds a qualitative mobility mechanism: growth does not become lived progress when stable jobs, networks, norms and perceived agency block movement into the middle class. It is a purposive community study from 2016, not a current prevalence estimate, representative regional poll or causal evaluation; its value is explanatory depth and a warning against reading macro indicators as complete social experience.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official World Bank publication pages, main report PDF and regional summary were retrieved and reviewed for the growth-perception disconnect, jobs and mobility, networks, social norms, public-sector aspirations and methodological implications; the PDF was hashed.
